title: AI Agents Working Together · Level 3
slo: Identify the parts of an AI agent and how multiple agents can collaborate.

exercises.question_text: Which part is an AI agent's brain for language understanding and reasoning?

options.text: A large language model
options.rationale: Correct. A large language model is the brain-like reasoning component.

options.text: A system prompt
options.rationale: A system prompt defines behavior. It does not perform language understanding and reasoning.

feedback.intrinsic: The agent would have guidance but no language-reasoning brain.
feedback.instructional: Instructions guide behavior; the language model understands and reasons.

options.text: A knowledge tool
options.error_type: Confuses the model with a tool
options.rationale: A knowledge tool retrieves information. It is not the component that reasons over language.
options.better_fit: This fits access to a search engine or database.

feedback.intrinsic: Information could be available without a way to interpret the question.
feedback.instructional: Knowledge tools find information; language models reason about language.

options.text: An action tool
options.rationale: An action tool performs external tasks. It does not supply language understanding.
options.better_fit: This fits sending an email or updating a calendar.

feedback.intrinsic: Work might be performed without understanding the request.
feedback.instructional: Action tools execute tasks; the language model provides language reasoning.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The large language model is the agent's brain for language work.

exercises.question_text: Which statements are true about action tools and multi-agent systems? Select all that apply.

options.text: Action tools can send emails
options.rationale: Correct. Sending email is an external task an action tool can perform.

options.text: Action tools can update calendars
options.rationale: Correct. Updating a calendar is another external action.

options.text: Specialized agents can collaborate on a workflow
options.rationale: Correct. Multi-agent systems coordinate specialized agents on shared work.

options.text: Knowledge tools directly control devices
options.rationale: Knowledge tools retrieve information. Device control is an external action.

feedback.intrinsic: A device-control request could be assigned to retrieval and never completed.
feedback.instructional: Knowledge tools find information; action tools perform tasks such as device control.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Action tools perform tasks, and specialized agents can collaborate.

exercises.question_text: A large language model helps an AI agent understand and reason over natural language.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The agent could not reliably work through a language request.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A large language model helps an agent understand and reason over natural language.

exercises.explanation: Correct! That is the language model's brain-like role.

exercises.question_text: An AI agent only answers questions and cannot use tools to automate tasks.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A request needing an email or calendar update could remain incomplete.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: AI agents can reason over language, use tools, and respond with appropriate action.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An AI agent can use tools to automate tasks.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The distinction between guidance and task execution is lost.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State what instructions guide first, then contrast that with what tools perform.

exercises.correct_answer: Instructions guide the agent's behavior but tools perform external tasks.
exercises.explanation: Instructions guide role and behavior, whereas tools interact with the world. The contrast distinguishes guidance from capabilities.

exercises.question_text: Which are examples of agent tools? Select all that apply.

options.text: A search engine
options.rationale: Correct. A search engine is a knowledge tool that provides information.

options.text: A database
options.rationale: Correct. A database can provide information to an agent.

options.text: A calendar updater
options.rationale: Correct. Updating a calendar is an external task performed through an action tool.

options.text: A system prompt
options.rationale: A system prompt defines role and behavior. It is not a capability for world interaction.

feedback.intrinsic: The agent would know how to behave but could not retrieve information or update a calendar.
feedback.instructional: Tools provide world-facing capabilities; instructions provide guidance.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Agent tools include both information and action capabilities.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between information access and databases becomes unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the category, state what it gives the agent, then provide the database example.

exercises.correct_answer: Knowledge tools give an agent access to information such as databases.
exercises.explanation: Knowledge tools give agents access to information, including database records. This distinguishes them from action tools.

exercises.question_text: An employee asks a travel assistant for policy details and then asks it to reschedule a meeting. Which choices correctly separate the needed agent parts? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a knowledge tool to find the policy
options.rationale: Correct. Policy details are information retrieved through a knowledge tool.

options.text: Use an action tool to change the calendar
options.rationale: Correct. Changing a calendar is an external task for an action tool.

options.text: Use instructions as the source of policy facts
options.rationale: Instructions define behavior, not current policy facts. Policy facts should come from an information source.
options.better_fit: This fits setting how the assistant should respond to policy questions.

feedback.intrinsic: The answer could omit actual policy details.
feedback.instructional: Use instructions for behavior and knowledge tools for information retrieval.

options.text: Use the language model as the calendar-changing tool
options.rationale: The language model understands the request. An action tool is required to change the calendar.
options.better_fit: This fits interpreting the requested calendar change.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting would remain unchanged despite understanding the request.
feedback.instructional: Language models reason over requests; action tools perform calendar changes.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Information retrieval and calendar updates require different kinds of tools.

exercises.question_text: A helpdesk designer needs an assistant to answer employee questions using current records in a company database. Which capability is the best fit?

options.text: A knowledge tool connected to the database
options.rationale: Correct. This gives the assistant access to the current records required for grounded answers.

options.text: An action tool that updates a calendar
options.rationale: Calendar updates are external actions. They do not retrieve current database records.
options.better_fit: This fits changing a meeting when that is requested.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant could change a meeting while remaining unable to answer from records.
feedback.instructional: Current database records are information, so use a knowledge tool.

options.text: A system prompt that sets a friendly tone
options.rationale: A friendly tone affects behavior. It does not connect the assistant to current records.
options.better_fit: This fits defining the assistant's response style.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant may sound friendly while lacking current evidence.
feedback.instructional: Instructions set tone; knowledge tools provide information access.

options.text: A large language model without information access
options.rationale: A language model can understand questions. Without access, it cannot retrieve current company records.
options.better_fit: This fits the agent's language-reasoning component.

feedback.intrinsic: The answer may not be grounded in current records.
feedback.instructional: Reasoning is useful, but current data requires a knowledge tool.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Database-connected knowledge access is the best fit for current records.

exercises.question_text: The system prompt that defines an agent's role and behavior is its ___.

parts.text: The system prompt that defines an agent's role and behavior is its

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name reasoning or a capability rather than behavior guidance.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use agent instructions for the system prompt that acts as a job description.

exercises.explanation: Agent instructions are the system prompt that gives the agent its role and behavior.

exercises.question_text: A software application that uses generative AI, tools, and context to take action is an ___.

parts.text: A software application that uses generative AI, tools, and context to take action is an

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The term would name either underlying technology or a group instead of the application.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use AI agent for the digital assistant that reasons, uses tools, and acts.

exercises.explanation: An AI agent is one application that combines language reasoning, tools, and action.

options.text: Specialized agents that collaborate on work
options.rationale: Correct. A multi-agent system is a group of specialized agents working together.

options.text: One agent's system prompt
options.rationale: A system prompt guides one agent's behavior. It is not a group of collaborating specialists.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would have guidance but no collaborating specialists.
feedback.instructional: A multi-agent system contains multiple agents with coordinated responsibilities.

options.text: One knowledge tool for a database
options.error_type: Confuses a group with a tool
options.rationale: A database connection is one information capability. A multi-agent system is a group of agents.

feedback.intrinsic: The design would provide information access without dividing work among specialists.
feedback.instructional: A knowledge tool retrieves facts; multi-agent systems coordinate agents.

options.text: One language model that predicts text
options.error_type: Confuses a system with a model
options.rationale: A language model is one reasoning component. A multi-agent system includes multiple collaborating applications.
options.better_fit: This fits an agent's large language model.

feedback.intrinsic: A complex workflow would be left with one component instead of specialists.
feedback.instructional: Distinguish one model from a coordinated group of agents.

exercises.explanation: Correct! A multi-agent system brings together specialized agents.
